claims.text: most prevalent nonviral STI worldwide; about 2.6 million people in the US
claims.quote: Trichomoniasis is estimated to be the most prevalent nonviral STI worldwide, affecting approximately 2.6 million persons in the United States

claims.text: 70 to 85 percent have minimal or no symptoms; untreated infections might last months to years
claims.quote: The majority of persons who have trichomoniasis (70%–85%) either have minimal or no genital symptoms, and untreated infections might last from months to years

claims.text: women: discharge can be diffuse, malodorous or yellow-green, with or without vulvar irritation (body, table, FAQ smell)
claims.quote: women with trichomoniasis sometimes have vaginal discharge, which can be diffuse, malodorous, or yellow-green with or without vulvar irritation

claims.text: men sometimes have urethritis, epididymitis or prostatitis
claims.quote: Men with trichomoniasis sometimes have symptoms of urethritis, epididymitis, or prostatitis

claims.text: passes during penile-vaginal sex and among women who have sex with women via vaginal fluids or fomites
claims.quote: it is readily passed between sex partners during penile-vaginal sex or through transmission of infected vaginal fluids or fomites among women who have sex with women

claims.text: male partners of women with trichomoniasis are likely to be infected (FAQ men)
claims.quote: Male partners of women with trichomoniasis are likely to have infection

claims.text: most recurrences likely result from reinfection, such as from an untreated partner
claims.quote: A recurrent infection can result from treatment failure (antimicrobial-resistant T. vaginalis or host-related problems), lack of adherence, or reinfection from an untreated sex partner. ... most recurrent infections likely result from reinfection.

claims.text: NAATs are highly sensitive, detecting more infections than wet mount; FDA-cleared NAATs report sensitivities of about 95 to 100 percent
claims.quote: NAATs are highly sensitive, detecting more T. vaginalis infections than wet-mount microscopy among women ... with a sensitivity of 95.3%–100% and specificity of 95.2%–100%

claims.text: wet mount sensitivity 44 to 68 percent vs culture; follow a negative wet mount with a more sensitive test when possible
claims.quote: it has low sensitivity (44%–68%) compared with culture ... More highly sensitive and specific molecular diagnostic options are available, which should be used in conjunction with a negative wet mount when possible.

claims.text: nitroimidazoles are the only class with clinically demonstrated efficacy
claims.quote: The nitroimidazoles are the only class of medications with clinically demonstrated efficacy against T. vaginalis infections.

claims.text: women: metronidazole 500 mg twice daily for 7 days; men: metronidazole 2 g single dose (key points, table, FAQ, citable summary)
claims.quote: Recommended Regimen for Trichomoniasis Among Women Metronidazole 500 mg 2 times/day for 7 days Recommended Regimen for Trichomoniasis Among Men Metronidazole 2 g orally in a single dose

claims.text: tinidazole 2 g single dose is the alternative for women and men; CDC 2021 regimens list only metronidazole and tinidazole
claims.quote: Alternative Regimen for Women and Men Tinidazole 2 g orally in a single dose

claims.text: cure rates about 84 to 98 percent for recommended metronidazole regimens and 92 to 100 percent for tinidazole (table and figure 2)
claims.quote: In randomized clinical trials, recommended metronidazole regimens have resulted in cure rates of approximately 84%–98%, and the recommended tinidazole regimen has resulted in cure rates of approximately 92%–100%

claims.text: women with HIV: metronidazole 500 mg twice daily for 7 days; single 2 g dose less effective in a trial
claims.quote: a single dose of metronidazole 2 g orally was less effective than 500 mg 2 times/day for 7 days

claims.text: multidose treatment more effective, particularly for symptomatic women or those with prior trichomoniasis
claims.quote: Multidose oral metronidazole is more effective than single-dose treatment, particularly for women who are symptomatic or have a history of T. vaginalis

claims.text: metronidazole gel not recommended: does not reach therapeutic levels in urethra and perivaginal glands, less effective
claims.quote: Metronidazole gel does not reach therapeutic levels in the urethra and perivaginal glands. Because it is less efficacious than oral metronidazole, it is not recommended.

claims.text: abstain until everyone has completed treatment and symptoms resolved
claims.quote: Providers should advise persons with T. vaginalis infections to abstain from sex until they and their sex partners are treated (i.e., when therapy has been completed and any symptoms have resolved).

claims.text: concurrent partner treatment is vital for preventing reinfection; current partners referred for treatment (key points, partners, red-flag box, FAQ)
claims.quote: Concurrent treatment of all sex partners is vital for preventing reinfections. Current partners should be referred for presumptive therapy.

claims.text: test for other STIs including HIV, syphilis, gonorrhea and chlamydia
claims.quote: Testing for other STIs, including HIV, syphilis, gonorrhea, and chlamydia, should be performed for persons with T. vaginalis.

claims.text: sexually active women retested about 3 months after treatment because reinfection is common
claims.quote: Because of the high rate of reinfection among women treated for trichomoniasis, retesting for T. vaginalis is recommended for all sexually active women approximately 3 months after initial treatment

claims.text: metronidazole resistance in 4 to 10 percent of cases of vaginal trichomoniasis
claims.quote: Metronidazole resistance occurs in 4%–10% of cases of vaginal trichomoniasis

claims.text: persistent infection without reexposure: clinicians can request CDC drug-resistance testing
claims.quote: For persons who are experiencing persistent infection not attributable to reexposure, clinicians should request a kit from CDC to perform drug-resistance testing

claims.text: women reexposed: repeat the same 7-day regimen
claims.quote: If treatment failure occurs in a woman after completing a regimen of metronidazole 500 mg 2 times/day for 7 days and she has been reexposed to an untreated partner, a repeat course of the same regimen is recommended.

claims.text: women not reexposed: metronidazole or tinidazole 2 g once daily for 7 days
claims.quote: If no reexposure has occurred, she should be treated with metronidazole or tinidazole 2 g once daily for 7 days.

claims.text: men reexposed: single 2 g dose again; men not reexposed: metronidazole 500 mg twice daily for 7 days
claims.quote: he should be retreated with a single 2-g dose of metronidazole. If he has not been reexposed, he should be administered a course of metronidazole 500 mg 2 times/day for 7 days.

claims.text: documented resistance: can include metronidazole or tinidazole 2 g daily for 7 days
claims.quote: Treatments for infections demonstrating in vitro resistance can include metronidazole or tinidazole 2 g daily for 7 days.

claims.text: 1.5-fold increased risk of HIV acquisition and more HIV vaginal shedding (key points, complications, FAQ)
claims.quote: T. vaginalis infection is associated with a 1.5-fold increased risk for HIV acquisition and is associated with an increase in HIV vaginal shedding

claims.text: among women with HIV, higher risk of pelvic inflammatory disease
claims.quote: Among women with HIV infection, T. vaginalis infection is associated with increased risk for PID.

claims.text: pregnancy: premature rupture of membranes, preterm birth, small-for-gestational-age infants
claims.quote: T. vaginalis infection among pregnant women is associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, particularly premature rupture of membranes, preterm delivery, and delivery of infants who are small for gestational age

claims.text: treatment reduces symptoms and might reduce transmission; cures infection
claims.quote: Treatment reduces symptoms and signs of T. vaginalis infection, cures infection, and might reduce transmission.

claims.text: data lacking on whether screening and treating women without symptoms in high-prevalence settings reduces harms
claims.quote: data are lacking regarding whether screening and treatment for asymptomatic trichomoniasis in high-prevalence settings for women at high risk can reduce any adverse health events

claims.text: symptomatic pregnant people tested and treated at any stage
claims.quote: Symptomatic pregnant women, regardless of pregnancy stage, should be tested and treated.

claims.text: metronidazole low fetal risk; tinidazole avoided in pregnancy (body and FAQ)
claims.quote: Although metronidazole crosses the placenta, data indicate that it poses a low risk to the developing fetus ... Thus, tinidazole should be avoided for pregnant women

claims.text: condoms are the best prevention; douching not recommended
claims.quote: the best way to prevent genital trichomoniasis is through consistent and correct use of condoms (external or internal) ... Douching is not recommended because it might increase the risk for vaginal infections, including trichomoniasis

claims.text: testing recommended for women seeking care for vaginal discharge (red-flag box)
claims.quote: Diagnostic testing for T. vaginalis should be performed for women seeking care for vaginal discharge.

claims.text: caused by Trichomonas vaginalis, a protozoan (single-celled) parasite; sexually transmitted
claims.quote: Trichomoniasis (or "trich") is a very common STI caused by infection with trichomonas vaginalis (a protozoan parasite).

claims.text: people without symptoms can still pass it on
claims.quote: People with trich can pass the infection to others, even if they do not have symptoms.

claims.text: women: lower genital tract (vulva, vagina, cervix or urethra); men: inside the penis (urethra)
claims.quote: In women, the infection is most commonly found in the lower genital tract (vulva, vagina, cervix, or urethra). In men, the infection is most commonly found inside the penis (urethra).

claims.text: women may notice itching, burning, redness or soreness, discomfort when peeing, discharge with a fishy smell
claims.quote: Itching, burning, redness or soreness of the genitals ... Discomfort when peeing ... A clear, white, yellowish, or greenish vaginal discharge (i.e., thin discharge or increased volume) with a fishy smell

claims.text: men may notice itching or irritation inside the penis, burning after peeing or ejaculating, discharge
claims.quote: Itching or irritation inside the penis ... Burning after peeing or ejaculating ... Discharge from the penis

claims.text: not common to infect other body parts like hands, mouth or anus
claims.quote: It is not common for the parasite to infect other body parts, like the hands, mouth, or anus.

claims.text: cannot be diagnosed on symptoms alone; a laboratory test confirms it
claims.quote: It is not possible to diagnose trich based on symptoms alone. Your healthcare provider can examine you and a laboratory test will confirm the diagnosis.

claims.text: reinfection in about 1 in 5 people within 3 months after treatment
claims.quote: Reinfection occurs in about 1 in 5 people within 3 months after receiving treatment.

claims.text: reinfection often from a partner who was not treated (FAQ)
claims.quote: This can happen if you have sex without a condom with a person who has trich. To avoid reinfection, your sex partners should receive treatment at the same time.

claims.text: talk about STI risk before sex with a new partner and ask a clinician whether to be tested (prevention; red-flag box: ask about testing after any new partner even without symptoms)
claims.quote: talk about the potential risk of STIs before having sex with a new partner ... Ask them if you should get tested for trich or other STIs.

claims.text: BV: normal lactobacilli replaced by high levels of anaerobic bacteria
claims.quote: BV is a vaginal dysbiosis resulting from replacement of normal hydrogen peroxide and lactic-acid–producing Lactobacillus species in the vagina with high concentrations of anaerobic bacteria

claims.text: BV discharge thin, milklike; fishy odor
claims.quote: Homogeneous, thin discharge (milklike consistency) that smoothly coats the vaginal walls ... A fishy odor of vaginal discharge before or after addition of 10% KOH (i.e., the whiff test)

claims.text: BV: itch can occur
claims.quote: BV NAATs should be used among symptomatic women only (e.g., women with vaginal discharge, odor, or itch)

claims.text: BV treated with metronidazole or clindamycin
claims.quote: Metronidazole 500 mg orally 2 times/day for 7 days OR Metronidazole gel 0.75% one full applicator (5 g) intravaginally, once a day for 5 days OR Clindamycin cream 2%

claims.text: BV linked to sexual activity but whether it results from a single sexually transmitted pathogen is unknown (FAQ)
claims.quote: BV is associated with having multiple male sex partners, female partners ... a new sex partner, lack of condom use ... whether BV results from acquisition of a single sexually transmitted pathogen is unknown.

claims.text: yeast usually Candida albicans
claims.quote: VVC usually is caused by Candida albicans but can occasionally be caused by other Candida species or yeasts.

claims.text: yeast discharge thick, curdy
claims.quote: Signs include vulvar edema, fissures, excoriations, and thick curdy vaginal discharge.

claims.text: vulvar itching is a typical symptom; none of the symptoms is specific
claims.quote: Typical symptoms of VVC include pruritus, vaginal soreness, dyspareunia, external dysuria, and abnormal vaginal discharge. None of these symptoms is specific for VVC.

claims.text: azole antifungal treatment
claims.quote: Treatment with azoles results in relief of symptoms and negative cultures in 80%–90% of patients who complete therapy.
